outcome: No source dated after 26 January 2024 settles or moves any of the three parts the bullet names (the main gap for uncountable first-order theories, for AECs, and for ℵ1-saturated models of a countable theory); the in-window items are neighbouring results on other questions (a stable forking counterexample credited to GPT-5.6 Sol, OpenAI's CH-based AEC obstruction about a categoricity threshold, and several Shelah, Laskowski, Moreno and Baldwin papers), and the 2025 FWF project page still describes Main Gap-type results in other contexts as not established.
problem_asks: The bullet names one conjecture by its instances: the main gap conjecture, given as 'e.g.' for three kinds of class. Unpacked: (1) the main gap for uncountable first-order theories, i.e. first-order theories T not assumed countable, with a gap dichotomy on the number of isomorphism types of models (the frozen statement does not spell out the dichotomy; the readings in the literature are Shelah's counting dichotomy in cardinals κ); (2) the main gap for abstract elementary classes (AECs), i.e. the same kind of gap dichotomy for AECs; (3) the main gap for ℵ1-saturated models of a countable first-order theory, i.e. the dichotomy restricted to the class of ℵ1-saturated models of a countable T. The statement gives no cardinal conditions and no precise dichotomy, and 'e.g.' means these three are instances of the conjecture rather than three separate problems. Shelah's established theorem for countable complete first-order T is context, not one of the three parts asked for.

events.what_happened: Shelah's Main Gap theorem for countable complete first-order theories, as it appears in Classification Theory and the Number of Non-isomorphic Models (Sh:c), first edition 1978, revised edition North-Holland 1990 (Studies in Logic vol. 92). Moreno (arXiv 2308.07510) cites it as Shelah [Sh:c, Ch. XII, Thm 6.1]; the nLab and Harrington–Makkai exposition describe the same result. I did not open the book or any copy of the theorem. The 1978 date and the claim that the first edition contains this theorem come from search summaries and from citations, not from a text I read.
events.revisions: Revised edition North-Holland 1990 (Studies in Logic vol. 92), per search results.
events.delivers: For countable complete T: if T is not classifiable (not superstable, or deep, or with DOP or OTOP), then I(κ,T) = 2^κ for every uncountable κ; if T is shallow superstable without DOP or OTOP, then I(ℵα,T) < i_ω1(|α|) for every α > 0 (as the search summaries and Moreno state it). Restricted to countable T.
events.remains: Item (1) of problem_asks (uncountable T), item (2) (AECs), and item (3) (ℵ1-saturated models of a countable T), none of which is a countable first-order T.

checked_by.who: Saharon Shelah (author); later expositors Harrington and Makkai
checked_by.qualification: Author of the theorem; expository paper by Harrington and Makkai in Notre Dame Journal of Formal Logic (1985)
checked_by.what_they_did: Shelah published the proof in the book; Harrington and Makkai published an exposition (not read by me)

events.direction: Establishes the gap dichotomy for countable complete T. This affirms the gap in the countable case, which the bullet's 'e.g.' does not list.

events.what_happened: Shelah, 'The spectrum problem I: ℵε-saturated models, the main gap'. Search summaries describe it as proving the main gap for ℵε-saturated models of a complete first-order T (with superstability, NDOP and the decomposition into well-founded trees of small models). Not opened: the only source is a MaRDI portal record (portal.mardi4nfdi.de, Q788713) seen in search results, and the venue is not confirmed by me.
events.delivers: Main gap for ℵε-saturated models of a complete first-order T (per search summaries), a restricted version of the countable-T theorem; not uncountable T in general.
events.remains: Items (1), (2) and (3) of problem_asks: ℵ1-saturated models are not ℵε-saturated, and nothing is said about AECs or uncountable T in general.
events.doubts: Not read; the description rests on search summaries of the record only.
events.direction: Affirms the gap for ℵε-saturated models of countable T.

events.what_happened: Harrington and Makkai, 'An exposition of Shelah's main gap: counting uncountable models', Notre Dame Journal of Formal Logic 26(2), 1985. Search summaries say it covers the main gap for countable complete T and states that Shelah completed the full proof. The projecteuclid page returned empty content to my fetch, so I did not read the exposition.
events.delivers: Exposition of the countable-T main gap (per search summaries). It adds no new result that I could confirm.
events.doubts: Not read, so the description of what it covers is unverified.

events.what_happened: Grossberg and Hart, 'The classification theory of excellent classes', Journal of Symbolic Logic 54 (1989) 1359–1381. Grossberg's CMU profile (search result, not opened) says he and Hart proved a case of Shelah's main gap conjecture for atomic models of a first-order theory, which is the excellent-class setting.
events.delivers: A main gap for excellent classes of atomic models of a first-order theory (under the excellence hypotheses, which I did not read). Restricted to excellent classes; does not cover uncountable T in general, AECs in general, or ℵ1-saturated models.
events.remains: Items (1), (2) and (3) of problem_asks, except as an analogue for the atomic-model class.

checked_by.what_they_did: Published the paper (article not read by me)

events.direction: Affirms the gap for excellent classes, an analogue of the first-order case (Grossberg's own description: a case of the conjecture for atomic models).

events.what_happened: Hyttinen and Shelah, 'Main gap for locally saturated elementary submodels of a homogeneous structure', arXiv math/9804157, first submitted 15 April 1998; J. Symbolic Logic 66(3) (2001) 1286–1302. The arXiv abstract page is opened: 'We prove a main gap theorem for e-saturated submodels of a homogeneous structure.'
events.delivers: A main gap for e-saturated (locally saturated) elementary submodels of a homogeneous structure. Its class is not the class of ℵ1-saturated models of a countable T, nor an AEC, nor uncountable first-order T in the bullet's sense; the abstract gives no cardinal assumptions and I did not read the body.
events.remains: Items (1), (2) and (3) of problem_asks, as the class in the theorem differs from each.
events.direction: Affirms a main gap for a related but different class (analogue).

events.what_happened: Shelah, 'On what I do not understand (and have something to say), model theory', arXiv math/9910158, submitted 28 October 1999; Math. Japon. 51 No. 2 (2000) 329–377 (per the abstract page). This is a list of open problems, not a result. §4 'Relatives of the main gap' has Problem 4.1(1) 'Prove the main gap for the class of ℵ1-saturated models', Problem 4.1(2) 'Prove the main gap for the class of ℵ0-saturated models', Problem 4.5 'Prove the main gap for K_T' (K_T the intersection of reducts of models of expansions T1 of T with |T1| ≤ 2^ℵ0), and Problem 4.7 'Prove the main gap for uncountable T', with the note that the difficulty is the lack of primary models over nonforking triples. The discussion after 4.1 says the work in [Sh:c] 'seems to solve it' except for the lack of regular types. The live problem list may differ from this 1999 text; I read the arXiv HTML extraction, not the journal version.
events.delivers: Nothing is established; the event is a statement of the open problems (items 1 and 3 appear as Problems 4.7 and 4.1(1)). I found no AEC main-gap problem in §4 of the HTML extraction; the non-elementary classes material is in §6, which the extraction did not reach in full.
events.direction: Records the three parts as open problems in 1999; no direction on the answer.

events.what_happened: Grossberg and Lessmann, 'Abstract decomposition theorem and applications', arXiv math/0509707, first submitted 29 September 2005; Contemporary Mathematics 380 (2005) 73–108. Opened abstract page: under assumptions of a well-behaved forking-like notion, regular types and prime models for an AEC K, a decomposition theorem holds and 'implies a main gap result for the class K'. Named settings: ℵ0-stable first-order theories, excellent classes of atomic models, and submodels of a large sequentially homogeneous ℵ0-stable model.
events.delivers: A main gap for AECs satisfying the stated hypotheses (regular types, prime models, forking-like notion), in named settings. It is an AEC main gap under extra hypotheses, not the general AEC conjecture; the hypotheses are the ones the bullet's AEC case does not assume.
events.remains: The AEC main gap without the extra hypotheses (item 2); uncountable first-order T in general (item 1); ℵ1-saturated models of a countable T (item 3).

checked_by.qualification: Refereed volume in a standard series
checked_by.what_they_did: Published the paper (2005); text not read beyond the abstract

events.doubts: The authors' hypotheses (regular types, prime models) are exactly what the 1999 problem list says is missing for ℵ1-saturated models, so the result does not reach that case on its own terms.
events.direction: Affirms a main gap for AECs under added hypotheses (partial, analogue-type result for the AEC part).

events.what_happened: Shelah and Vasey, 'Categoricity and multidimensional diagrams', arXiv 1805.06291 (2018 by arXiv identifier), published in Journal of the European Mathematical Society 26(7) (2024), per search summaries. Search summaries describe it as proving, under a proper class of strongly compact cardinals (and a weak GCH for AECs with amalgamation), the eventual categoricity conjecture. Not opened.
events.revisions: Journal publication 2024 (JEMS), revised February 2024 per a search summary.
events.delivers: Eventual categoricity for AECs under the stated large-cardinal and weak-GCH hypotheses. This is a different AEC conjecture from the main gap; it does not count models in the gap dichotomy.
events.remains: All of problem_asks; in particular it leaves the AEC main gap open (no statement of the gap dichotomy in what I could read).

checked_by.who: Journal of the European Mathematical Society referees

events.direction: Affirms eventual categoricity for AECs under large cardinals; a different question from the main gap.

events.what_happened: Espíndola, 'A proof of Shelah's eventual categoricity conjecture and an extension to accessible categories with directed colimits', arXiv 1906.09169, first submitted 21 June 2019 (v1 titled 'A topos-theoretic proof of Shelah's eventual categoricity conjecture for abstract elementary classes', under GCH and a measurable cardinal per the search summary); latest version v7 dated 13 April 2022. The arXiv abstract page I opened says the proof is 'in ZFC' for AECs, and that the accessible-categories extension assumes the Singular Cardinal Hypothesis.
events.revisions: v1 21 Jun 2019 (topos-theoretic, conditional on GCH and a measurable, per search summary); later retitled; v7 13 Apr 2022 (ZFC claim).
events.delivers: Claims eventual categoricity for AECs in ZFC (per the latest abstract). A different conjecture from the main gap; it does not address item (1), (2) or (3) of problem_asks.
events.doubts: I found no journal acceptance, referee report, errata or expert review of the ZFC version in searches; the status of the 2019 conditional argument and the 2022 ZFC claim is unresolved in what I read. I did not read the paper's body.
events.direction: Claims to affirm the eventual categoricity conjecture for AECs; a different question from the main gap.

events.what_happened: Moreno, 'Shelah's Main Gap and the generalized Borel-reducibility', arXiv 2308.07510. Opened abstract page: addresses the Friedman–Hyttinen–Kulikov conjecture on Borel reducibility of the Main Gap; under cardinal assumptions κ = λ⁺ = 2^λ and 2^ℵ0 ≤ λ = λ^ℵ1, isomorphism of models of a non-classifiable T′ lies strictly above that of a classifiable T under Borel reducibility; a second part states a forcing result for countable first-order theories (analytic co-analytic or analytically complete isomorphism). The abstract says the paper answers the FHK conjecture, without saying whether fully or partly. No journal publication found.
events.revisions: v1 15 Aug 2023; v2 5 Dec 2023; v3 1 Oct 2024; a v4 dated 29 Sep 2026 is reported by the abstract-page extraction (not verified by me).
events.delivers: Under κ = λ⁺ = 2^λ and 2^ℵ0 ≤ λ = λ^ℵ1, a Borel-reducibility comparison between classifiable and non-classifiable T, for the isomorphism relation. This is a descriptive-set-theoretic analogue of the Main Gap, not a count of models, and its cardinal assumptions are set-theoretic. It does not address items (1)–(3) as stated.
events.remains: Items (1), (2) and (3) of problem_asks: the paper's dichotomy is about Borel reducibility, not the number of models, and it is conditional on cardinal arithmetic.
events.time_since_posted: about 3 years 2 months (from v1, 15 Aug 2023, to 13 Oct 2026)
events.doubts: The conditional scope: the main theorem needs cardinal assumptions. The abstract says it 'answers' the FHK conjecture without saying in full. A 2026 paper by Feldman and Moreno (arXiv 2603.09510) also works in this line but its statement is for inaccessible κ; I did not read either body, so whether the 2023 result covers the whole FHK conjecture is unresolved here.
events.direction: Analogue: under set-theoretic assumptions, a Borel-reducibility dichotomy comparable to the Main Gap. Does not count models in cardinals.

events.what_happened: Baldwin, Laskowski and Shelah, 'When does ℵ1-categoricity imply ω-stability?', arXiv 2308.13942, submitted 26 August 2023; Model Theory 3 (2024) 801–823 (DOI 10.2140/mt.2024.3.801, per an arXiv listing seen in search). Search summary: an ℵ1-categorical atomic class with a model of size (2^ℵ0)+ is ω-stable. Not opened.
events.delivers: Per search summary: for an atomic class, ℵ1-categoricity with a model of size (2^ℵ0)+ forces ω-stability. This is about atomic classes of countable T, not uncountable T, AECs or ℵ1-saturated models.
events.direction: Neighbouring: a categoricity/stability result for atomic classes of countable T; does not bear on the gap dichotomy as stated.

events.what_happened: Baldwin, Laskowski and Shelah, 'An analogue of U-rank for atomic classes', arXiv 2502.00984, submitted 3 February 2025 (only version listed). Opened abstract page: for a countable complete first-order T, the class At of atomic models: if some type tp(d/a) is unranked, there are 2^ℵ1 pairwise non-isomorphic models in At of size ℵ1; if every type has finite rank, the rank is fully additive and every finite tuple is dominated by an independent set of realizations of pseudo-minimal types. The abstract does not mention the Main Gap, AECs or ℵ1-saturated models.
events.delivers: For atomic models of countable complete first-order T: an unranked type gives 2^ℵ1 non-isomorphic atomic models of size ℵ1; the finite-rank case gives a rank analogue. It counts models in a cardinal, the kind of quantity the gap concerns, but for atomic models of a countable T, not for uncountable T, AECs or ℵ1-saturated models.
events.remains: Item (1) (uncountable T, the atomic models here are of a countable T), item (2) (AECs), item (3) (ℵ1-saturated models are not atomic models).
events.doubts: The count of models at ℵ1 is a quantity of the same type the gap concerns, but the class is atomic models of a countable T, so it is an analogue for the atomic class. Reasons to read it either way are in summary.
events.direction: Counts models at ℵ1 for atomic classes of countable T: an unranked type forces the maximal number 2^ℵ1 of atomic models at ℵ1. The count is of a different class from the bullet's.

events.what_happened: Shelah, 'Twins: non-isomorphic models forced to be isomorphic. Part I', arXiv 2505.02088, v1 4 May 2025, v2 16 May 2025, v3 2 July 2025; published in Monatshefte für Mathematik 208(4) (2025) 751–790 per the HUJI record seen in search (not opened). The arXiv abstract page I opened says 'This is part of the classification and {Main Gap} program', and that for theories with the independence property non-isomorphic models become isomorphic in an extension by a forcing that adds no new ω-sequence.
events.delivers: Sufficient conditions under which non-isomorphic models of a (usually countable) complete first-order T become isomorphic after a forcing that adds no new sets of ordinals or collapses cardinals; for IP theories, when the forcing adds no new ω-sequence. The result is about forcing-isomorphism, not counting models in cardinals.

checked_by.what_they_did: Published the paper (2025 per the HUJI record; not read by me)

events.direction: Self-described as part of the Main Gap programme; the result is a forcing-isomorphism phenomenon, which neither affirms nor refutes the gap.

events.what_happened: Laskowski and Ulrich, 'Equivalents of NOTOP', arXiv 2505.00844, submitted 1 May 2025; Journal of Symbolic Logic (DOI 10.1017/jsl.2025.10135, online 4 Sep 2025 per search). Opened abstract page: in countable superstable T, NOTOP is equivalent to V-DI; under NOTOP every model is atomic over an independent tree of countable elementary substructures; NOTOP implies PMOP without using NDOP (verifying a claim in Shelah's book, Ch. XII). The abstract says the work is 'within the context of countable, superstable theories'.
events.delivers: Characterisations of NOTOP and structure of models under NOTOP, for countable superstable first-order T. Part of the countable-T classification machinery that the countable Main Gap already uses; it does not address uncountable T, AECs or ℵ1-saturated models.
events.direction: Neighbouring: characterises a key notion (NOTOP) of the countable-T Main Gap; does not bear on the three parts asked.

events.what_happened: Feldman and Moreno, 'Fodor space in generalized descriptive set theory', arXiv 2603.09510, v1 10 March 2026, v2 23 May 2026. Opened abstract page: for an inaccessible κ, if T has fewer than κ non-isomorphic models of size κ and T′ is unstable or superstable but non-classifiable, then isomorphism of models of T continuously reduces to isomorphism of models of T′ (on the space of regressive functions in κ^κ). The paper body was not readable to me.
events.delivers: A continuous-reducibility result for isomorphism relations, for inaccessible κ, under a few-models hypothesis on T. It is a descriptive analogue of the FHK-type question, not a count of models for the bullet's three classes.
events.doubts: Body not read; the abstract's hypothesis (fewer than κ models of size κ, inaccessible κ) is not the bullet's setting.
events.direction: Analogue: continuous reducibility under inaccessible κ; does not count models in the gap sense.

events.what_happened: Mutchnik, 'Reducing stable forking dependence to finitely many pregeometries', arXiv 2607.09069, v1 10 July 2026, v3 28 September 2026. Opened abstract page: in finite-rank supersimple theories, the stable-forking instability corresponds to a pregeometry, and the author shows the set of matroids G_n can be chosen finite in each rank; Peretz had proved rank 3 and the argument is extended to n > 3. The abstract does not mention the main gap.
events.delivers: A reduction of the finite-rank supersimple case of the stable forking conjecture to finitely many matroids. It concerns simple theories, not the stable main gap, and does not refute or prove the conjecture in general.
events.doubts: Body not read; the abstract says Peretz's rank-3 proof 'does not extend as stated' and claims an existence theorem for n > 3.
events.direction: Neighbouring: a partial step in the stable forking conjecture (simple theories), not the main gap.

events.what_happened: Freitag and Mutchnik, 'A counterexample to the stable forking conjecture', arXiv 2609.00436, submitted 31 August 2026 (v1; 21 pages; CC BY 4.0; math.LO, math.QA). Opened abstract page: 'Using ChatGPT 5.6, we find a counterexample to the stable forking conjecture', answering a question of Hart, Kim and Pillay (1996). The arXiv HTML extraction (WebFetch, not my own reading of the text) gives Section 1.1: 'This is an AI-generated result proven with the help of GPT-5.6 Sol.' The extraction does not show any mention of the main gap, Shelah's main gap, or AECs; the extraction was truncated partway through Section 4.1. A search summary of the paper names the counterexample as the theory of an infinite-dimensional vector space over the division ring of fractions of the quantum graph algebra of the random graph; the body I could read does not confirm this wording.
events.revisions: v1 31 Aug 2026 only, as far as I saw.
events.delivers: A counterexample to the stable forking conjecture, a conjecture about simple first-order theories (Hart–Kim–Pillay 1996), per the abstract. It refutes a simple-theory conjecture; it does not touch the stable main gap or any of items (1)–(3) as stated, and it is about a different class of theories.
events.remains: All of problem_asks: the paper does not discuss the main gap (per the extraction, nothing on the main gap, AECs or uncountable T).
events.doubts: Not peer reviewed. A search summary says MathWorld reported no independent external verification as of 7 Sep 2026, and a tracker entry lists the verification status as 'Unreviewed' (search results, not opened). The authors' own statements about the authorship of the proofs are not consistent with each other on the page (see disputes). I did not verify the mathematics.
events.direction: Refutes the stable forking conjecture for a simple theory (per the abstract). Against the conjecture named in its title; neither for nor against the main gap.
events.object: Per the abstract, a counterexample to the stable forking conjecture. A search summary identifies the theory as the theory of an infinite-dimensional vector space over the division ring of fractions of the quantum graph algebra of the random graph. This specific description was not confirmed in the text I could read. Its status as explicit or non-constructive is not stated in what I read.

systems.name: GPT-5.6 Sol
systems.what_it_did: Per Section 1.1 (as extracted): the result is 'an AI-generated result proven with the help of GPT-5.6 Sol'; the authors 'prompted ChatGPT to construct a counterexample to the stable forking conjecture with a detailed series of prompts'; the title-page footnote says 'the arguments in this paper were based on proofs generated using JF's ChatGPT account'. The same section says the proofs 'have been written entirely by the authors, and no AI tool was used in the actual writing of this manuscript', and that 'AI was used for proofreading, with the edits performed and evaluated manually by the authors'. Load-bearing for the counterexample (the authors say it would unlikely have been found without generative AI). Not load-bearing for the main gap; this paper does not treat the main gap.
systems.basis_quote: This is an AI-generated result proven with the help of GPT-5.6 Sol.

systems.name: ChatGPT 5.6
systems.what_it_did: The abstract credits ChatGPT 5.6 with finding the counterexample. This is the same model family as GPT-5.6 Sol in Section 1.1; I have recorded it as a separate string because the abstract uses it. The later pass should decide whether the two strings name one system.
systems.basis_quote: Using ChatGPT 5.6, we find a counterexample to the stable forking conjecture.

events.what_happened: OpenAI's public openai/math repository, released 6 October 2026, lists under the 'Mathematical logic' discipline (per a secondary blog, kingy.ai) a family 'Shelah's eventual categoricity conjecture' with 2 manuscripts. The CONTENTS.md entry numbered 240 is titled 'Shelah's eventual categoricity and the prescribed-threshold obstruction', with the preprint 'A CH obstruction to a prescribed categoricity threshold' (manuscript date-stamped 24 September 2026 in its path). The Lean docs page lean/docs/240.md (opened) states: under CH the formalized result 'refutes the proposed transfer of categoricity down to the Hanf threshold', via an AEC in a countable relational language with Löwenheim–Skolem number ℵ0, with two non-isomorphic models at ℶ_ω2 = h(ℵ0) and categorical in every cardinal at least ℶ_{(2^ℵ1)+}. It says the example imposes no amalgamation, joint embedding, tameness or no-maximal-models assumption. The page says a later canonical-point obstruction and a separate eventual-categoricity theorem are not included in this formalization.
events.revisions: The repository states that corrections and revisions are recorded as new versions. Three manuscripts were reportedly withdrawn the day after release (per a secondary aggregator, not verified by me); I did not identify whether any of them is in this family.
events.delivers: Under CH, an AEC (countable relational language, LS number ℵ0, no amalgamation or tameness) with two non-isomorphic models at ℶ_ω2 and categoricity at every cardinal ≥ ℶ_{(2^ℵ1)+}. This refutes a proposed transfer of categoricity down to the Hanf threshold. It is a counterexample to a categoricity-threshold proposal, not a result on the gap dichotomy of the number of models in the three classes, and it is conditional on CH.
events.remains: All of problem_asks: the result is about categoricity thresholds, not the gap, so items (1), (2) and (3) are untouched as stated; the AEC item is the only one a reader could connect to it, and that connection is a scope call for the later pass.

It shows the proposed categoricity transfer to the Hanf threshold fails. The page does not say whether the construction is explicit or non-constructive.

disputes.summary: Freitag and Mutchnik's stable-forking paper states both that 'the arguments in this paper were based on proofs generated using JF's ChatGPT account' (title-page footnote, as extracted) and that the proofs 'have been written entirely by the authors, and no AI tool was used in the actual writing of this manuscript' (Section 1.1, as extracted). Who produced the mathematics is therefore stated two ways in the same paper. Stable forking is not the main gap, so this matters here only as a precedent for how AI credit is phrased.

A Substack post dated 8 Oct 2026 (siliconreckoner) alleges that OpenAI's 6 Oct 2026 release contains a result whose proof strategy and specific notation are identical to a preliminary version of a paper 'uploaded to ChatGPT on September 8, 2026', and cites arXiv 2610.10072. That arXiv record is 'Invariant Primes in Lubin-Tate Space and Hovey-Strickland at Every Height' by Chenglong Ma (v1 7 Oct 2026), which does not mention AECs, eventual categoricity, OpenAI or ChatGPT. The cited link therefore does not support the allegation, the preliminary version is not identified, and the allegation is unverified. It concerns the eventual-categoricity family, not the main gap.

summary: I found no source dated after 26 January 2024 that settles, or moves a quantity named in, any of the bullet's three parts: the main gap for uncountable first-order theories, for AECs, and for ℵ1-saturated models of a countable theory. The countable first-order main gap is an established theorem (Shelah, Sh:c; the ℵε-saturated case in Sh:131), and the bullet's 'e.g.' cases lie beyond it; Shelah's 1999 problem list (arXiv math/9910158, opened in its HTML extraction) records the ℵ1-saturated case (Problem 4.1(1)), the ℵ0-saturated case (4.1(2)) and uncountable T (4.7) as open, and the discussion after Problem 4.1 says the work in [Sh:c] 'seems to solve it' except for the lack of regular types. The AEC part rests on partial results: Grossberg–Hart (1989) for excellent classes, Hyttinen–Shelah (1998/2001) for e-saturated submodels of a homogeneous structure, and Grossberg–Lessmann (2005) for AECs under regular-type and prime-model hypotheses. I could not open a primary statement of Shelah's AEC main-gap conjecture (Sh:300 and the 2009 introduction, arXiv 0903.3428, do not state it on the pages I could reach). The 2025 FWF project 'Classification over a predicate' (opened) says Main Gap-type results 'are conjectured in other contexts in model theory, but none have been fully established', which is a 2025 statement that the question is still open, though it concerns classification over a predicate. Among the in-window events, two carry AI credit and one is a close call on scope. (1) Freitag and Mutchnik (31 Aug 2026) report a counterexample to the stable forking conjecture 'using ChatGPT 5.6'; the arXiv HTML extraction gives 'an AI-generated result proven with the help of GPT-5.6 Sol' (Section 1.1). It is about simple theories and does not mention the main gap, so it is recorded as a discounted, different question, and its AI role is load-bearing for that question. (2) OpenAI's 6 Oct 2026 openai/math release lists an entry 240 'Shelah's eventual categoricity and the prescribed-threshold obstruction' and a companion 'Eventual categoricity for abstract elementary classes'. The Lean docs page (opened) says that under CH the formalized result refutes a proposed transfer of categoricity down to the Hanf threshold, via an AEC with two non-isomorphic models at ℶ_ω2 and categoricity above ℶ_{(2^ℵ1)+}. That is about categoricity thresholds, not the gap dichotomy. The authors credit 'an unreleased internal OpenAI model' in general terms. The companion preprint's PDF was not readable to me, and the Lean page does not say whether the proof is sorry-free. (3) Baldwin–Laskowski–Shelah (arXiv 2502.00984, Feb 2025) shows that an unranked type gives 2^ℵ1 atomic models at ℵ1 for a countable T. This is a count in a cardinal, which is the quantity the gap concerns, but for atomic classes, not the bullet's classes. The other in-window items are analogues or neighbouring work: Moreno's Borel-reducibility papers (2023, conditional on cardinal arithmetic; a 2026 Feldman–Moreno paper for inaccessible κ), Shelah's 'Twins' (May 2025, self-described as part of the Main Gap programme but about forcing-isomorphism), Laskowski–Ulrich on NOTOP (May 2025, countable superstable), and Mutchnik's finite-pregeometry reduction (Jul 2026, stable forking). No review, verification or citation of any of these bears on the bullet's three parts that I could find. Close calls: whether the OpenAI entry 240 should count as a move in the AEC part, since both it and the AEC main gap concern AEC categoricity; my reading is that eventual categoricity and the main gap are different conjectures and the result does not touch the gap's count of models. Whether the BLS 2025 ℵ1 count moves the gap for uncountable T: it counts atomic models of a countable T, so I record it as an analogue. Whether the countable-T main gap should be treated as 'settling' the bullet's 'e.g.' cases: I read the three listed classes as the bullet's content, and the countable theorem does not cover them. AI involvement: AI credit appears in two in-window items (Freitag–Mutchnik, and OpenAI's repository for entry 240 and the companion). No source I read names an AI system for the main gap itself, and for every item where I read only an abstract or landing page I set none_found true on that basis, which is a limit of what I read. The Wikipedia bullet is not cited in the frozen revision (page.wiki:392), and the live article's list was truncated before the bullet, so I could not confirm the live wording or its citation.
competing_reading: Read the OpenAI entry 240 family as a live AEC result on the bullet's second part. Shelah's AEC main gap and eventual categoricity both concern how categoricity and the number of models behave in AECs, and a result that refutes a categoricity-threshold transfer under CH moves the AEC picture. On that reading the bullet has an in-window AEC event with AI credit, and the judging pass should weigh it. The counter-reading, which I hold: the claim concerns categoricity thresholds, not the count of models that the gap dichotomy describes, so it does not change what the bullet asks for. A second competing reading concerns Baldwin–Laskowski–Shelah (Feb 2025): an unranked type forcing 2^ℵ1 atomic models at ℵ1 is exactly the maximal-count side of a gap dichotomy, so a reader could take it as a move on item (1). The counter-reading is that it concerns atomic models of a countable T and so is an analogue. A third reading treats Shelah's countable main gap (1978/1982) as settling the bullet's 'e.g.' content; the bullet's three listed classes are not countable first-order T, so that reading does not hold.
what_would_settle_it: (a) The text of Shelah's AEC main-gap conjecture as stated in Sh:300 or the forthcoming AEC classification book, to fix item (2) exactly. (b) The Lean file ComparatorChallenges/CHObstruction.lean and the status of 'sorry' in it, plus the readable PDFs of OpenAI's 'A CH obstruction to a prescribed categoricity threshold' and 'Eventual categoricity for abstract elementary classes', to see what the companion proves and whether it is sorry-free. (c) Expert reading of entry 240 and the companion, by named AEC specialists (e.g. Vasey, Boney, Grossberg, Shelah's own group), and a public record of whether they accept the CH obstruction. (d) The preliminary version the Substack says was uploaded to ChatGPT on 8 Sep 2026, which would settle the priority allegation; arXiv 2610.10072 is the wrong paper. (e) The full text of Feldman–Moreno (arXiv 2603.09510) and Moreno (arXiv 2308.07510) to see whether the FHK conjecture is established in full or only under cardinal assumptions, and whether either addresses uncountable T. (f) The Freitag–Mutchnik PDF text and the reconciliation of its two authorship statements, plus an independent check of the counterexample, to fix the AI attribution for the stable-forking result; this is not the main gap, so it would not change the bullet's record but would fix the AI-credit string.
